meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 16 (Multi-Select): Community, Governance & Security Policy
meta.format: multi_select: questions use the 'answers' array (multiple correct options). Some include an 'All of the above' option that is only correct when every other option is.

questions.question: Which statements about MCP's governance roles are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Maintainers steward specific areas (SDKs, docs, Working Groups) with write access to their repos
Core Maintainers can veto Maintainer decisions by majority vote and appoint or remove Maintainers
Lead Maintainers (BDFL) can veto any decision and appoint or remove Core Maintainers
Corporate seats guarantee each member company one Core Maintainer
All of the above

questions.explanation: Membership is individual and merit-based — there are explicitly NO company-reserved seats, which sinks D and the all-of-the-above option.

questions.question: Which licensing/legal facts about the MCP project are true? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The project is established as a Series of LF Projects, LLC
Code and specification contributions use Apache License 2.0
Documentation (excluding specifications) is CC BY 4.0
Contributors retain copyright — no assignment to the project is required
All of the above

questions.explanation: All four facts come straight from the governance page's General Project Policies — a legitimate 'All of the above'.

questions.question: Which reports are IN scope under the MCP security policy? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: An authorization bypass caused by an SDK bug
Token leakage stemming from a specification-level flaw
A parsing crash reachable through the Streamable HTTP transport
A malicious local stdio server hanging the client that spawned it (no remote reachability, no sandbox escape)
All of the above

questions.explanation: Stdio-peer-only DoS is the canonical out-of-scope case — the stdio transport is not a sandbox and peers share a trust boundary. A–C are squarely in scope.

questions.question: Which disclosure-process statements are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Reports go through GitHub Security Advisories (private reporting) on the affected repository
Public issues, discussions, and pull requests must not be used for security reports
Maintainers coordinate cross-SDK so fixes and advisories ship together when a shared pattern is affected
CVEs are assigned via GitHub's CNA in the GHSA workflow
All of the above

questions.explanation: The full disclosure pipeline as documented — every statement holds, so E is correct too.
